metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Peru

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Peru using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of students within schools across participating countries and economies, and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names (e.g., TOTWGT or W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were used, so analysts should consult the PISA 2022 technical documentation/Reader’s Guide for the precise weighting and variance estimation approach. Plausible values and scaling are handled within the OECD PISA scoring pipeline; this factsheet presents scaled scores on the creative thinking 60-point scale and associated uncertainty (95% confidence intervals) rather than detailing the PV/estimation mechanics.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because this document is a country factsheet summarizing published PISA 2022 creative thinking results rather than reporting an original student-level empirical model with explicit PV estimation steps. Missing-data handling is not reported because the factsheet focuses on descriptive comparisons and correlations/variance decomposition using OECD’s already-produced estimates, without detailing the underlying scoring/estimation procedures for missing responses. For full methodological transparency on PV estimation and missing data treatment, the OECD PISA 2022 technical documentation and Reader’s Guide should be consulted.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment results for Peru, reporting the analytic group of 15-year-old students who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science and for whom creative thinking results are available in the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The factsheet does not provide additional inclusion/exclusion rules beyond the standard PISA assessment participation and OECD’s scoring pipeline; it also notes that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard issues (asterisks) but does not indicate such a restriction for Peru.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for Peru for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Peru’s mean creative thinking score is 23 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average of 33. The factsheet reports proficiency distributions (47% at Level 3 or above; 10% at Level 5 or 6) and relative strengths/weaknesses across ideation processes and domain contexts using difficulty-adjusted “relative success” differences. It also highlights within-Peru gaps: socio-economic status is a strong predictor (explaining 19% of variation in creative thinking), and gender differences are limited (girls do not significantly outperform boys overall). Uncertainty is presented via 95% confidence intervals, and the document notes that some countries/economies with asterisks require caution due to unmet sampling standards.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (a descriptive reporting document) rather than an empirical ML study. As such, it does not train or evaluate machine learning models, does not specify PV handling or missing-data procedures at the level of an analysis pipeline, and does not report model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) for predictive targets. Therefore, main_findings and confounders_identified are intentionally left empty to avoid fabricating an ML-based analytic framework that is not present in the provided text.
